message.content:
### Building a New Desktop PC – A Step‑by‑Step Guide  

Below you’ll find everything from choosing parts to installing your first OS. Whether you’re building a gaming rig, an editing workstation, or just a reliable everyday machine, this checklist will keep you organized and help avoid common pitfalls.

---

#### 1️⃣ Define Your Purpose & Budget  
| Use Case | Typical Specs | Rough Price Range |
|----------|---------------|-------------------|
| **Gaming** | GPU: RTX 3060/3070; CPU: Ryzen 5/7 or Intel i5/i7; RAM 16–32GB | $800–$1500+ |
| **Content Creation / Video Editing** | GPU: RTX 4060 Ti/4070; CPU: Ryzen 9 or Intel i9; RAM 32–64GB | $1200–$2500+ |
| **Office / Light Workstation** | Integrated graphics or low‑end discrete GPU; CPU: Core i3/Ryzen 5; RAM 8–16GB | $400–$700 |
| **Budget Build** | Entry‑level GPU + mid‑range CPU; minimal peripherals | <$500 |

*Tip:* Use [PCPartPicker](https://pcpartpicker.com/) to compare prices, check compatibility, and read reviews before buying.

---

#### 2️⃣ Gather Components  
> *All items below assume a standard ATX tower.*

| Component | What It Does | Suggested Brands / Models |
|-----------|--------------|----------------------------|
| **CPU** | Central processing unit | AMD Ryzen 5 7600x, Intel Core i5‑13600K |
| **Motherboard** | Connects all hardware | MSI B650M PRO‑VDH WIFI, ASUS TUF Gaming Z690‑WiFi D4 |
| **RAM** | Memory for multitasking | Corsair Vengeance LPX 16GB DDR5‑6000 |
| **GPU** | Graphics rendering | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Ti, AMD Radeon RX 6700 XT |
| **Storage** | SSD/HDD for OS & data | Samsung 970 EVO Plus 1TB NVMe M.2 |
| **Power Supply Unit (PSU)** | Supplies power | EVGA SuperNOVA G5 750W Gold |
| **Case** | Enclosure with airflow | NZXT H510, Fractal Design Meshify C |
| **Cooling** | Keeps temperatures down | Noctua NH-U12S redux, Cooler Master Hyper 212 RGB |
| **Operating System** | Software platform | Windows 11 Home OEM, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS |
| **Peripherals** | Input/output devices | Keyboard, mouse, monitor, speakers/headphones |
| **Tools** | Screwdrivers, anti‑static wristband | Phillips #0 screwdriver set, static mat |

> ⚠️ **Compatibility Check:** Verify socket type (e.g., AM5 vs LGA1700) and form factor (ATX/Micro‑ATX). Ensure PSU wattage covers total draw plus headroom (~20% extra).

---

#### 3️⃣ Prepare Workspace  
1. Clean, flat surface.  
2. Anti‑static mat or work on non‑conductive floor.  
3. Keep screws separate per component (use labeled containers).  
4. Have a small flashlight handy if working inside tight spaces.

---

#### 4️⃣ Assemble Inside Out  

##### 4.1 Install Power Supply  
- Place PSU at bottom rear (or top depending on case design).  
- Secure with two screws.  
- Route cables through designated holes—keep them tidy.

##### 4.2 Mount Motherboard Standoffs  
- Align standoff positions with motherboard screw holes.  
- Tighten lightly; don’t overtighten as it may damage board.

##### 4.3 Insert CPU  
- Lift the CPU socket lever.  
- Match the triangle marker on the processor to the one on the socket.  
- Drop gently into place then lock lever back down.

##### 4.4 Apply Thermal Paste & Attach Cooler  
- If cooler doesn’t come pre‑applied, spread ~½ teaspoon of paste onto center of CPU.  
- Position cooler over CPU, align mounting brackets.  
- Tighten screws evenly in cross pattern until secure.

##### 4.5 Install RAM  
- Snap memory slots open.  
- Line up notch with slot key.  
- Push firmly until click indicates proper seating.

##### 4.6 Mount Storage Drives  
- For M.2 SSD: Slide drive into M.2 slot at ~30° angle, press straight down, tighten screw.  
- For SATA HDD/SSD: Slot into bay, connect SATA data cable to motherboard, attach SATA power cable from PSU.

##### 4.7 Fit GPU  
- Remove corresponding expansion slot cover(s).  
- Align PCI‑Express x16 slot with card’s connector.  
- Press downward until fully seated.  
- Secure with screws to case bracket.  
- Connect required PCI‑E power connectors from PSU.

##### 4.8 Wire Everything Together  
| Cable Type | Where to Plug In | Notes |
|-------------|------------------|-------|
| **24‑pin ATX** | Motherboard main header | Main power supply |
| **8‑pin EPS** | Motherboard CPU power header | Some CPUs need additional power |
| **PCI‑E 8‑Pin** | GPU | Usually requires 450W+ GPUs |
| **SATA Data** | Drive → Motherboard | One port per SATA device |
| **SATA Power** | Drive → PSU | From dedicated SATA power rail |
| **USB Headers** | Front panel USB ports | Refer to manual for layout |
| **Audio Header** | Front audio jack | Standard 10‑pin header |
| **Front Panel Connectors** | Power button, reset, LEDs | Follow motherboard diagram |

> 🔌 **Cable Management Tip:** Bundle excess lengths together using Velcro ties or zip ties. This improves airflow and makes future upgrades easier.

##### 4.9 Double‑Check All Connections  
- Confirm no loose screws or dangling wires.  
- Make sure fans spin when powered on.

##### 4.10 Close the Case  
- Reinstall side panels.  
- Tighten all screws securely but not overly tight to avoid damaging panels.

---

#### 5️⃣ First Boot & Basic Setup  

1. **Connect Monitor, Mouse, Keyboard** to front/rear I/O ports.  
2. **Plug in Power Cord**, switch PSU ON.  
3. **Press Power Button** on case.  
4. Enter **BIOS/UEFI** immediately (usually `Del` or `F2`).  
   - Set boot priority: SSD > DVD/CD-ROM > Network.  
   - Enable XMP profile for RAM speed.  
   - Disable unused onboard devices (if desired).  
   - Save changes (`Esc` ➜ “Save & Exit”).  
5. Let system POST (power‑on self test); you should see manufacturer logo and progress bar.  
6. Once booted, install operating system:
   - Create bootable USB via Rufus or BalenaEtcher.  
   - Select correct partition scheme (MBR/GPT) matching UEFI mode.  
   - During installation, format SSD as NTFS (Windows) or ext4 (Linux).  
7. After OS installs, plug in internet connection.  
8. Update chipset, GPU, and other driver packages.  
9. Install essential software: web browser, Office suite, antivirus, etc.

---

#### 6️⃣ Post‑Build Checklist  

| Item | Why It Matters |
|------|----------------|
| **Thermal Monitoring** | Use HWMonitor or SpeedFan to ensure temps stay <70°C under load. |
| **Stress Test** | Run Prime95 or Cinebench R23 to confirm stability. |
| **Backup Plan** | Configure cloud backup or external drives early. |
| **Clean Up Dust** | Periodically wipe vents and replace filters. |
| **Keep Documentation** | Store receipts, serial numbers, warranty info. |

---

#### 7️⃣ Common Pitfalls & How to Avoid Them  

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| **Short Circuit** | Always unplug PSU during internal work. Wear anti‑static wrist strap. |
| **Overheating** | Proper fan orientation (intake at front/top, exhaust at rear/back). |
| **Insufficient Power** | Double‑check PSU rating against estimated consumption. Add headroom. |
| **Component Damage** | Handle each part carefully; use plastic tweezers for tiny pins. |
| **Boot Failure** | Verify BIOS settings, reseat GPU/memory, update firmware. |

---

#### 8️⃣ Resources & Further Reading  

- **Video Tutorials**  
  - *Linus Tech Tips*: “Building a PC” series  
  - *JayzTwoCents*: Detailed component explanations  
- **Forums**  
  - r/buildapc (Reddit) – great Q&A community  
  - Tom's Hardware Forums – troubleshooting threads  
- **Software Utilities**  
  - CPU-Z, GPU-Z – identify installed hardware  
  - CrystalDiskInfo – health status of storage drives  
  - Speccy – full system overview  

---

### Quick Reference Cheat Sheet  

```
[ ] PSU -> Motherboard (24-pin)
[ ] PSU -> Motherboard (EPS 8-pin)
[ ] PSU -> GPU (PCI-E 8-pin)
[ ] Motherboard -> GPU (PCI-E slot)
[ ] Motherboard -> SSD (NVMe slot)
[ ] Motherboard -> SATA HDD/SSD (data + power)
[ ] Motherboard -> Front panel headers (USB, Audio, Power Switch)
[ ] Fans -> PSU (via Molex/Fan headers)
```

Feel free to tweak the above according to your exact needs! Happy building 🚀
